description: Wi-Fi Alliance launched the Wi-Fi 6 standard in September 2019. There are many key differences between Wi-Fi 5 and Wi-Fi 6. The Wi-Fi 5, or 802.11ac, standard was introduced in 2013 by the Wi-Fi Alliance. The technical standard is now 13 years old. However, various devices still ship with support for Wi-Fi 5. The Wi-Fi 6, 802.11ax, standard is relatively new. The Wi-Fi Alliance introduced Wi-Fi 6 in September 2019, making it only seven years old. Most flagship smartphones ship with support for Wi-Fi 6. However, Wi-Fi 7 is now the most advanced standard, which was introduced in 2024. Wi-Fi 6 is much better at handling high-bandwidth tasks, delivering a maximum theoretical speed of up to 9.6Gbps. However, real-world speeds could be lower depending on the devices. Yet, it is better for playing competitive games online, watching high-definition (HD) content, and downloading multiple large files simultaneously.
title: Wi-Fi 5 vs Wi-Fi 6: What Is the Difference?

description: Smartphone displays have come a long way in a short period of time. LCD panels, which once dominated the market, have been phased out in most segments in favour of more advanced display technologies. Today, buyers can choose from AMOLED, OLED, pOLED, and other types. Meanwhile, high-end smartphones are also increasingly advertised with another term — LTPO. It is often mentioned alongside 120Hz refresh rates and always-on displays. However, LTPO is not simply another type of screen panel, but a backplane technology that helps a display dynamically adjust its refresh rate depending on what is being shown.
title: What Is LTPO Display Technology? How It Works, Benefits and Drawbacks Explained
